_note: Hand-reviewed prompt pack for the Spanish definition and expression prompts.
Mined from the 2025 corpus (13,518 definition cells, 8,590 expression cells)
by the same method as the Chinese pack; the measured basis for every value is
recorded in observations/v3-patch-crew-C.md.
Spanish is the most regular of the four target languages: capital-to-full-stop
holds in 99.9% of the shipped definition glosses (13,505 of 13,518; the 13
exceptions are all migrated:2025 cells, one of them a correctly punctuated
interrogative adverb). The gloss also opens with a
content word rather than an article (determiner-initial is 4.0%, against 35.8%
in English and 36.9% in German). Both are deliberate register, so the pack
pins them.
COVERAGE METHOD for fixed_renderings_table: each percentage is the share of
definition cells whose DANISH definition contains the left-hand formula (for
the frame rows, the `der` form: `person der`, `noget der`) and whose target
gloss contains the right-hand rendering. Stated because a reviewer read the
`der/som` label as the denominator and could not land on the value: the
`der|som` denominator gives 60.0 / 36.5 / 58.9% for noget and 76.5 / 81.1 /
73.2% for person (EN/DE/ES), i.e. the whole table would shift, not one row.
Re-derived 2026-08-26: the `der`-form numbers reproduce exactly.
Danish text in the worked examples is HAND-AUTHORED in DDO's editorial style.
No DDO source text is stored in this file.
allowed_scripts: Latin letters including accented vowels and ñ, Spanish punctuation including the inverted marks, and Arabic digits
orthography_rules: Write Spanish with its accents and with ñ: 18.4% of shipped lemmas carry an accented character, and an unaccented form is a spelling error, not a variant. Begin every `gloss` with a capital letter and end it with a single full stop -- 99.9% of shipped glosses do. Open the `gloss` with a content word, not with an article (determiner-initial is 4.0%).
lemma_charset_rule: Spanish letters including accented vowels and ñ, plus spaces. No article, no digits, no quotation marks; hyphens are effectively absent (0.04%).
punctuation_rule: ASCII punctuation plus the inverted marks the language requires. Commas 42.8% of glosses, semicolon 13.7% for a short synonym tail. Colons and slashes are effectively absent (under 0.4%); do not introduce them.
pos_vb: Give the full infinitive in -ar, -er or -ir, adding -se only when the sense is genuinely reflexive (6.6% of verb lemmas). 66.5% of shipped verb lemmas end that way.
pos_sb: Give the bare singular noun with no article (article-initial lemmas are 0.49%). A multiword noun lemma is normally built with `de` (13.7% of multiword lemmas).
pos_function: Open the `gloss` with `Se usa`, `Se emplea` or `Indica` and name the function (`se`-initial covers 31.5% of function-word glosses, 86.3% for interjections).

definitions.gloss: Acción de mover algo hacia uno mismo usando fuerza.
Corriente de aire frío que se mueve por una habitación, por ejemplo desde una puerta abierta.
Cualidad característica de una persona o cosa, a menudo fácil de reconocer.

fixed_renderings_table: fx              -> por ejemplo (51.9%, and it beats `p. ej.` 79:1)
det at ...      -> el acto de ... (28.4%) / la acción de ...
om person       -> refiriéndose a una persona (31.2%)
med hensyn til  -> en términos de / respecto a
anti_patterns: bad lemma el coche -> an article in the lemma; article-initial lemmas are 0.49% of the corpus -> good lemma coche

bad gloss una corriente de aire frio que se mueve por una habitacion -> a determiner opening, two missing accents, no capital and no full stop -> good gloss Corriente de aire frío que se mueve por una habitación.
bad lemma sufijo nominal -> a grammatical label instead of a concept (V4 lemma rule 2) -> good: name the meaning the element contributes

bad gloss Acción de mover algo hacia uno mismo usando fuerza, que en física se llama tensión. -> over-explaining past the Danish definition (V4 gloss rule 2) -> good gloss Acción de mover algo hacia uno mismo usando fuerza.
length_targets: lemma: one word 66.2% of cells, two 20.0%, three 11.3%. Median 9 characters, 90th percentile 17.
gloss: 11 words is the median, 21 the 90th percentile, 33 the 99th; above 25 words needs a reason. Exactly one sentence, capital letter to a single full stop.
lemma_allowed_set: Spanish letters including accented vowels and ñ, and spaces
gloss_allowed_set: Spanish letters including accented vowels and ñ, Spanish punctuation including the inverted marks, Arabic digits, the Danish letters æ ø å when a Danish word is named, and rarely a concise English word

fixed_expressions.gloss: Significa ser una persona de carácter fuerte capaz de imponerse.
Significa emocionarse muchísimo o perder por completo el control.
